title: One Screen Sprint
user: Two people at one keyboard who want an immediate competitive five-minute game with readable controls and a fresh procedural course each match.

evidence.quote_or_summary: Ask HN explicitly seeks browser games that are engaging, sensory, reaction-based, and exciting rather than turn-based or story-heavy; replies note weak web implementations and performance problems.
A live browser shooter’s HN play discussion reports that it loads on an iPhone and held a player’s attention for 20 minutes, validating fast browser action without an install.

recurrence: An explicit game-finder request defines a still-unmet browser use case, while real player feedback shows immediate browser action can hold attention when it loads cleanly.
current_workaround: Play Slither-like games alone, open a desktop multiplayer title, or use a browser shooter that requires a public server and network conditions.
incumbents_and_gap: Browser shooters serve remote play and arcade portals serve solo scores; simple same-keyboard action with guaranteed short matches is comparatively neglected.
smallest_useful_product: A two-player local side-view dash-and-grapple race. One player uses WASD, the other arrows; a procedurally assembled 75-second course changes each best-of-five match. Non-goals: guns, online matchmaking, chat, account profiles, or user-created levels.
success_measure: 70% of sessions finish a full best-of-five and 40% generate a second course without leaving the page.
monetization: free — it is a shareable zero-friction game; no ads should interrupt a 75-second round.
constraints: Test focus handling and key rollover; touch is not a v1 promise; use original art/sound; include seizure-safe effects settings.
why_distinct: It serves physical co-presence with one keyboard, not the much more common online shooter queue.
